Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:11:1.english: Unbeknownst to her - She did not know [about it] when it was written.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:11:2.hebrew: רבא ורבינא אמרו מקודשת - טעמייהו מפרש בפ"ק (לעיל קידושין דף ט:): מה יציאה לא בעינן כתיבה מדעתה, שהרי בעל כרחה מגרשה — אף הויה כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:11:2.english: Rava and Ravina say she is betrothed - Their reasoning is explained in the first chapter (above, Kiddushin 9b): Just as with regard to leaving through divorce, we do not require writing with her consent, for behold, he divorces her against her will; so too with regard to becoming betrothed, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:11:3.hebrew: אינה מקודשת - מה יציאה בעינן בכתיבת הגט דעת מקנה, דהיינו בעל שמקנה את האשה לעצמה בגט זה — אף הויה בעינן דעת מקנה, והיא האשה שמקנה את עצמה לבעל בשטר זה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:11:3.english: She is not betrothed - Just as with regard to leaving through divorce, we require in the writing of the bill of divorce the consent of the one who transfers — namely the husband, who transfers the woman to herself with this bill of divorce — so too with regard to becoming betrothed, we require the consent of the one who transfers, and that is the woman, who transfers herself to the husband with this document.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:12:1.hebrew: כהני תנאי - מקדש במלוה, דשמעתיה דרב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:12:1.english: Like these tanna’im - [Shall we say that] betrothing with a loan, which is Rav’s teaching, [is subject to a dispute between these tanna’im]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:12:3.hebrew: ואקדש אני לך - בשכר פעולתך, שהזהב משלה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:12:3.english: And I will be betrothed to you - In exchange for the wage of your labor, for the gold is hers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:13:1.english: That money - That he returns them to her after he has finished them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:13:2.hebrew: מכלל דת"ק אפילו אותו ממון נמי לא - בתמיה. כלומר, מכלל דכיון שעשאן דקאמר ר"מ, אף על פי שלא באו לידה — קא מתמה: אלא במאי בו מקדשא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:13:2.english: By inference, the first tanna [holds that] even that money is also not [required] - [This is said] in astonishment. That is to say, from the implication that [the statement] "once he has made them" which Rabbi Meir said [means] even though they have not come into her possession, [the Gemara] wonders: Rather, with what is she betrothed to him?

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:13:3.hebrew: אלא במקדש במלוה קמיפלגי - והכא מאי מלוה איכא? דקסברי כולהו: ישנה לשכירות מתחלה ועד סוף — כל פרוטה ופרוטה כשנגמרה, נתחייב בה בעל המלאכה לפועל בשכירות עשיית המלאכה. הלכך, כשמחזירן לה, ההוא הויא לה מלוה למפרע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:13:3.english: Rather, they disagree with regard to one who betroths with a loan - And here, what loan is there? For they all hold: [The obligation to pay] wages accrues from beginning to end — as each and every perutah's worth [of work] was completed, the employer became obligated for it to the worker as wages for performing the work. Therefore, when he returns them to her, that [debt] is a loan to her retroactively.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:1:1.english: And even an heir - [The heir] of the creditor.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:1:2.hebrew: מוחל - שהלוה לא נתחייב ללוקח כלום אלא מחמת המוכר, והרי מחלו אצלו. ר"מ לית ליה דשמואל, הלכך סמכה דעתה, ולא חיישינן דלמא אזיל ומחיל ליה. ורבנן אית להו דשמואל, הלכך לא סמכה דעתה, דסברה אזיל ומחיל ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:1:2.english: [Can] forgive - For the borrower did not become obligated to the purchaser at all except on account of the seller, and behold, he has forgiven it to him. Rabbi Meir does not hold in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel; therefore, her mind relies [upon it], and we are not concerned that he might go and forgive it to him. And the Rabbis hold in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel; therefore, her mind does not rely [upon it], as she reasons: He might go and forgive it to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:1:3.hebrew: אית להו דשמואל - דאי בעי, אזיל ומחיל ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:1:3.english: They hold in accordance with [the view of] Shmuel - For if he wishes, he [can] go and forgive him [the debt].

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:2:1.hebrew: והכא באשה קא מיפלגי - כלומר, אם היה מקנהו קרקע בדמי שטר זה, ודאי לא קנה המלוה את הקרקע, דלא סמכה דעתא דבעל קרקע. אבל באשה, סבר ר"מ דסמכה דעתה, דכיון דאיתתיה אנא — לא שביק לדידי ומחיל לאחריני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:2:1.english: And here they disagree with regard to a woman - That is to say, if [a landowner] were transferring land to him for the value of this note, certainly the creditor would not acquire the land, for the mind of the landowner does not rely [on it]. But in [the case of] a woman, Rabbi Meir holds that her mind relies [on it], for [she reasons:] "Since I am his wife, he will not leave me aside and forgive [the debt] to others."

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:3:1.hebrew: במעמד שלשתן - אמר לו כן, קנה. ואין טעם בדבר, דהא חד הוא מתלת מילי דשוינהו רבנן הלכתא בלא טעמא במס' גיטין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:3:1.english: In the presence of the three of them - [If] he said so to him, [the recipient] acquires [it]. And there is no reason for the matter, for this is one of three matters that the Sages established as halakha without a reason in Tractate Gittin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:4:1.hebrew: בפקדון - דאיתיה בעין, וסמכה דעתא דמקבל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:4:1.english: In [the case of] a deposit - For it is intact, and the mind of the recipient relies [upon it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:1.english: Let us say [this is subject to a dispute between] Tannaim - [Namely, with regard to] one who betroths [a woman] with a loan.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:2.hebrew: התקדשי לי בשטר - גרס, ולא גרס הכא בשטר חוב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:2.english: Be betrothed to me with a document - [This] is the reading, and one does not read here “with a promissory note.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:3.hebrew: ר' אלעזר אומר מקודשת - ואפי' אין בנייר שוה פרוטה, כדמפרש טעמא לקמן: אי משום דמקדש במלוה מקודשת, אי משום כדמשנינן לקמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:3.english: Rabbi Elazar says she is betrothed - And even if the paper does not have the value of a peruta, as [the Gemara] explains the reason below: whether because one who betroths with a loan is betrothed, or because of what we resolve further on.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:4.hebrew: אינה מקודשת - ואפי' הנייר שוה פרוטה, דלאו דעתה להתקדש בפרוטת הנייר, אלא במה דכתיבא ביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:4.english: She is not betrothed - And even if the paper is worth a peruta, for it is not her intent to become betrothed with the peruta of the paper, but rather with what is written in it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:5.hebrew: ר' אלעזר אומר מקודשת - ואפי' אין בנייר שוה פרוטה, כדמפרש טעמא לקמן: אי משום דמקדש במלוה מקודשת, אי משום כדמשנינן לקמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:5.english: Rabbi Elazar says she is betrothed - And even if the paper does not have the value of a peruta, as [the Gemara] explains the reason below: whether because one who betroths with a loan is betrothed, or because of what we resolve further on.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:5:6.english: [The court] appraises the paper - For her intention is also [directed] toward the paper.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:6:1.hebrew: קשיא דר"מ אדר"מ - דהא תניא לעיל: ״התקדשי לי בשטר חוב״ — ר"מ אומר: מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:6:1.english: [The statement] of Rabbi Meir is difficult in light of [another statement of] Rabbi Meir - For behold, it is taught above: “Be betrothed to me with a promissory note” — Rabbi Meir says: She is betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:6:2.english: Rather, is it not with a promissory note of hers - That he has a loan against her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:7:1.hebrew: בשטר שאין לו עדים עליו - שטר אירוסין קאמר, שכתב לה על הנייר: ״הרי את מקודשת לי״, ולא החתים עליו עדים, אלא מסרו לה בפני עדים. פלוגתא דר"מ ורבי אלעזר במסכת גיטין גבי גט, דקאמר ר' אלעזר: אע"פ שאין עליו עדים, אלא נתנו לה בפני עדים — כשר, שאין העדים חותמים על הגט אלא מפני תקון העולם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:7:1.english: With a document that has no witnesses on it - [He] means a document of betrothal, where he wrote to her on the paper: “Behold, you are betrothed to me,” and did not have witnesses sign on it, but rather delivered it to her in the presence of witnesses. [This is] the dispute of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Elazar in Tractate Gittin regarding a bill of divorce, as Rabbi Elazar says: “Even though it has no witnesses on it, but rather he gave it to her in the presence of witnesses, it is valid; for witnesses sign on a bill of divorce only for the betterment of the world.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:8:1.english: Effect severance - [This] renders it a scroll of severance.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:8:2.hebrew: מספקא להו בהאי אי כר"מ אי כרבי אלעזר - וסבירא להו דדעתה נמי אניירא, הלכך שמין כו'. ולפי התירוץ הזה, נראה בעיני דלא גרס בהא דרבנן "ואם לאו אינה מקודשת", אלא: "וחכ"א שמין את הנייר, אם יש בו שוה פרוטה מקודשת". ובאין שוה מידי לא איירי, משום דמספקא להו בההיא אי כר"מ אי כר' אלעזר. והשתא, ביש בו הוא דאתו לאיפלוגי — דאם יש בנייר שוה פרוטה, מקודשת בתורת כסף, דדעתייהו נמי אנייר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:8:2.english: They are uncertain regarding this, whether [the halakha is] in accordance with Rabbi Meir or in accordance with Rabbi Elazar - And they hold that her intention is also [directed] toward the paper; therefore, [the court] appraises, etc. And according to this resolution, it appears to me that the text should not read in this [statement] of the Rabbis: “And if not, she is not betrothed,” but rather: “And the Sages say: We appraise the paper: if it has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed.” And [the baraita] does not deal with [a case where it] is not worth anything, because they are uncertain in that [case] whether [the halakha is] in accordance with Rabbi Meir or in accordance with Rabbi Elazar. And now, it is [specifically] in [the case where] it has [the value of a peruta] that they came to disagree — for if the paper has the value of a peruta, she is betrothed by virtue of money, as their intention is also [directed] toward the paper.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:9:1.english: Where he wrote it - [Referring to] a document of betrothal [written] not for her sake.

Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:9:2.hebrew: יציאה בעינן לשמה - דכתיב (דברים כד) וכתב לה — לשמה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 48a:9:2.english: [Regarding] leaving, we require [that it be written] for her sake - For it is written: “And he shall write for her” (Deuteronomy 24:1) — [this means] it [must be] for her sake.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:1:1.hebrew: המוכר שטר חוב לחבירו וחזר ומחלו מחול - י"מ: היינו טעמא דמחלו מחול — משום דקנין שטר אינו אלא מדרבנן, ולא אלים להפקיע כח הראשון שלא יוכל למחול אותו. וכן משמע בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמז:), דקנין שטרות אינן אלא מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:1:1.english: "One who sells a promissory note to another, and went back and forgave it, it is forgiven" - Some explain: This is the reason that [if] he forgave it, it is forgiven — because the acquisition of a promissory note is only Rabbinic, and it is not powerful enough to nullify the power of the original [creditor] so that he would not be able to forgive it. And so it implies in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 147b), that the acquisition of promissory notes is only Rabbinic.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:4:1.hebrew: כי קאמר רב בפקדון אבל במלוה לא - וא"ת: אמאי לא קאמר דכ"ע כי קאמר רב אפילו במלוה, והכא מיירי במעמד שלשתן, וקמיפלגי בדשמואל דאמר: "אפי' יורש מוחל"; א"נ, סברי כשמואל, ובסמכה דעתה קא מיפלגי, וכדאמר לעיל? אלא מדלא קאמר הכי, שמע מינה דאפי' שמואל מודה דהמקנה לחבירו במעמד שלשתן ומחלו — אינו מחול. והא דקאמר לעיל: "המוכר שטר חוב לחבירו וחזר ומחלו — מחול" — היינו דוקא כשאין הלוה בפנינו בשעה שמכר לו את השטר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:4:1.english: When Rav said [this, it applies] to a deposit, but to a loan, no - And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] not say that everyone [agrees that] when Rav said [his ruling], [it applies] even to a loan, and here we are dealing with [a transfer in] the presence of all three parties, and they disagree regarding [the statement] of Shmuel, who said: "Even an heir can forgive [the debt]"; alternatively, they [both] hold in accordance with Shmuel, and they disagree regarding [whether] her mind relies [on collecting it], just as [the Gemara] said above? Rather, since [the Gemara] did not say this, learn from it that even Shmuel concedes that [in the case of] one who transfers [a debt] to another in the presence of all three parties, and [subsequently] forgave him, it is not forgiven. And that which [Shmuel] said above, "One who sells a promissory note to another and went back and forgave him, it is forgiven" — that is specifically when the debtor is not present before us at the time he sold him the promissory note.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:5:1.hebrew: שמין את הנייר - ודוקא אליבא דרבנן אמרי' דשמין את הנייר; אבל לר"מ, אפי' איכא בנייר שוה פרוטה — אינה מקודשת, דאמר: עדי חתימה כרתי הקידושין. וא"ת: לרבנן, אמאי שמין את הנייר? אפילו כי ליכא בנייר שוה פרוטה, מקודשת מספק כרבי אלעזר, דאמר: עדי מסירה כרתי! וי"ל: דלזה מהני: אם היה בו שוה פרוטה — מקודשת קידושין גמורין; אבל אם אינו שוה פרוטה — אינה מקודשת כי אם מספק, להצריכה גט אם נשאת לאחר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:5:1.english: "The court appraises the paper" - And [it is] specifically according to the Rabbis that we say that they appraise the paper; but according to Rabbi Meir, even if there is the value of a peruta in the paper, she is not betrothed, as he says: Signatory witnesses effect the betrothal. And if you say: According to the Rabbis, why do they appraise the paper? Even when there is not the value of a peruta in the paper, she should be betrothed out of doubt, in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, who says delivery witnesses effect [the betrothal]! And one can say that it is effective for this: If it had the value of a peruta, she is betrothed with a complete betrothal; but if it is not worth a peruta, she is not betrothed except out of doubt, to require her [to receive] a bill of divorce if she married another.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:6:1.hebrew: אילימא בשטר חוב דאחרים קשיא דר"מ אדר"מ - ואם תאמר: ומאי קושיא? לישני דלעיל מיירי דאמר ליה: "קני לך שטר וכל שיעבודיה", והכא מיירי דלא אמר ליה! וי"ל: שהיה תופס לדוחק, מאחר שהלשונות שוים, לומר שאינם בסיגנון אחד:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:6:1.english: "If we say [it is] a promissory note of others, [the statement] of Rabbi Meir is difficult in light of [another statement] of Rabbi Meir" - And if you say: What is the difficulty? Let [the Gemara] answer that above deals with [a case where] he said to her, "Acquire the document and all of its liens," and here deals with [a case where] he did not say [this] to her! And one can say: [The Gemara] considered it forced, since the wordings are identical, to say that they are not of the same manner.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:8:1.hebrew: ורבנן מספקא להו כו' - לפירוש זה, לא גרס במילתייהו "ואם לאו אינה מקודשת" — דהא אפילו ליכא בנייר שוה פרוטה צריכה גט מספק, דשמא עדי מסירה כרתי כר"א. דאי אמרת דאין צריכה גט — א"כ קאי כר"מ, דאמר עדי חתימה כרתי מכל וכל; וא"כ, מאי האי דקאמר: מספקא להו אי כר"מ, אי כר' אלעזר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 48a:8:1.english: "And the Rabbis are uncertain, etc." - According to this interpretation, one does not read in their [the Rabbis'] words: "And if not, she is not betrothed" — for even if there is not the value of a peruta in the paper, she requires a bill of divorce out of uncertainty, for perhaps witnesses to transmission effect [the betrothal], in accordance with Rabbi Elazar. For if you were to say that she does not require a bill of divorce, if so, [the ruling] stands in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says that signatory witnesses effect [the betrothal] completely; and if so, what is this that [the Gemara] says: "They are uncertain whether [the halakha is] in accordance with Rabbi Meir or in accordance with Rabbi Elazar"?
